title: Joinder, consolidation, and separate trials
summary: A court can coordinate related litigation or separate issues for trial without treating every procedural unit as one merged claim. These management choices seek efficiency while limiting prejudice and confusion.
notes: A shared courtroom or pretrial process does not necessarily merge separate actions for every purpose. Jurisdiction, appealability, and substantive rights require their own analysis.

sections.Meaning: A court can coordinate related litigation or separate issues for trial without treating every procedural unit as one merged claim. These management choices seek efficiency while limiting prejudice and confusion.
sections.How to work through the question: Distinguish joining parties and claims in one action, consolidating separate actions, ordering separate trials of issues, and multidistrict coordination. Identify the rule or statute and the effect on party rights and judgments.
